articleTitle: Superconducting quantum interference devices
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A brief overview is given of the fundamental principles governing the behaviour of Superconducting Quantum Interference Devices (SQUIDs). This includes the relevant superconducting theories and the quantum interference phenomenon. The structures and principles of operation of two classes of SQUIDs, RF and DC SQUIDs, are discussed and practical implementations and performance are given.

articleTitle: Feasibility of the fail-silent property in distributed computer control systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The concept of a fail-silent processing module makes it possible to take advantage of the ease with which redundant processing modules can be included in a cluster of processing modules of a distributed computer control system in order to implement hardware fault tolerance. The issues involved in implementing a fail-silent processing module by employing a set of sub-processors and a solution to the Byzantine generals problem are analyzed. It is concluded that this approach appears to provide a feasible basis for future practical implementations of a fail-silent processing module.

articleTitle: Wait time in meteor-burst communications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The design and implementation of meteor-burst communications systems are currently the subject of a great deal of research work. Most studies of the communications potential of the channel have concentrated on channel throughput. The question of how much data the channel can carry is an essential concern, but so too is the question of how long it will take to successfully send a message. This latter issue, wait time, has received considerably less attention, and is addressed by this paper. Results of simulations using data recorded by practical monitoring systems are presented, allowing a comparison of wait times amongst various combinations of data rates and message sizes. The meteor trail families contributing at these rates and sizes are identified.

articleTitle: Betroubaarheidsmodellering van stedelike radiale retikulasiestelsels met behoud van detail
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: UITTREKSEL 'n Metode word aangebied wat stedelike radiale retikulasiestelsels se betroubaarheidseienskappe met behoud van detail modelleer. Dit bevredig die behoeftes van die praktyk daarin dat die eienskappe van die samestellende komponente nie verlore gaan nie. Die gebruik van kansveranderlikes gee dit 'n groter mate van realisme teenoor metodes wat met gemiddelde waardes werk. Die metode gebruik 'n merkalgoritme en voorstellings (nl merke en boë) uit netwerkteorie, 'n onderafdeling van Operasionele Navorsing of optimeringswiskunde. Die besondere eienskappe van die maksimumvloei-algoritme maak dit geskik om die vloeikarakter van elektrisiteit te weerspieël. Dit stel die metode in staat om nie net primêre foute te hanteer nie maar om ook foute wat daaruit vloei te ontleed. Die voorgestelde metode gee aan beplanners die vermoë om die betroubaarheid van 'n nuwe stelsel of voorgestelde veranderings aan 'n bestaande stelsel voor implementering te evalueer.

articleTitle: A computer aided nodule detection algorithm for lung cancer diagnosis
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The development and operation of an algorithm for computer-aided diagnosis of lung cancer is described. The algorithm uses a tunable difference of averages edge detector and a template matching procedure in its operation of lung cancer nodule detection. Feature extraction is performed on the resulting correlation surface and suspected nodule sites are encircled in the final stage. Preliminary results of this detection scheme are included.

articleTitle: Factors affecting the prediction of commutating limits for a DC machine under varying speed and load conditions
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the difficulties associated with predicting and correcting the commutation of a D.C. machine. A theoretical model of the well known “black band” test is proposed. Further research on factors arising from the theoretical model will be considered in an effort to predict the commutation performance of the machine by the use of finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Optimization of the controller synthesis for three-phase inverter using space vector pulse-width-modulator
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper suggests a controller synthesis optimization for a three-phase inverter on the basis of the analysis of some space vector PWM details which are not given in [1, 2, 3] as well as of the dynamic behavior of the induction motors fed by the three-phase inverters. The equations for the output voltage harmonics content using Space Vector hodograph are derived.

articleTitle: A study of the simple regenerative snubber circuit
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The behaviour and characteristics of a simple regenerative snubber circuit, which is applied in a chopper circuit, are investigated. Mathematical descriptions for the switching transients are formulated and used to describe the limitations that the snubber circuit impose on the allowable switching frequency of the main power device. It is shown how the upper switching frequency limit is exactly determined by the snubber element sizes, the switching time of the main device and by the magnitude of the additional voltage and current stresses. The results are confirmed experimentally.

articleTitle: Glare in sports lighting
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Proposed CIE recommendations for glare in sports lighting are reformulated and their implications for practical design are analysed. Mounting height is crucial for limiting glare and other aspects such as floodlighting characteristics and aiming angles are also important.

articleTitle: Modellering van die pompfunksie van die hart
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: SAMEVATTING Modellering van die pompfunksie van die hart kan op verskeie maniere gedoen word. Die model wat hier bespreek word, berus op die end-sistoliese elastiese kenmerke van die ventrikel (Ees) en die elastiese kwaliteit van die arteriële bed (Ea). Ees is 'n lading onafhanklike indeks van miokardiale kontraktiliteit en Ea verteenwoordig arteriële intree impedansie. Data in hierdie laboratorium toon dat hierdie parameters die ventrikel en sy las akkuraat modelleer, beide onder fisiologiese en patologiese omstandighede.

articleTitle: On high rate maximum runlength limited (O, k) blocked line codes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The essential parameters of runlength constrained codes are defined, together with a brief discussion of the properties of these codes. An overview of previous work done on (0, k) codes is also presented. A new algorithm is introduced for the enumeration of (0, k) block codes. This algorithm is further compared in terms of complexity and speed to previously published algorithms. A new high rate code is presented and compared to previously published codes.

articleTitle: Unified distortion compensation in power network
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper deals with simultaneous compensation of all components of non-active power, as well as stochastic distortions, unbalanced load and load leveling. A new control algorithm is proposed allowing elimination of any non-active components with practically no delay time.

articleTitle: Adaptive control of a TCR for hybrid compensators using a cost function minimization approach
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An energy related approach for the interpretation and subsequent compensation of electrical power networks is introduced. It is proposed that optimum supply utilization is brought about by the correct time distribution of the energy drawn from the source, and supplied to a load. A time-domain based, digital adaptive control technique for TCR's, for implementation in proposed hybrid compensation schemes, is further described. An ‘optimum reactive current’ is calculated in the time-domain and a linear extrapolation predictor is further implemented in real-time to estimate future values of the firing angles for the thyristors in such an energy redistribution device (i.e. compensator).

articleTitle: Thundercloud electrification and its discharge to ground: Assessments of observations and postulates
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The mechanisms responsible for the build up of charge within the thundercloud and the resultant negative lightning flash to ground are discussed from the standpoint of well-established physical principles and parameters, particularly those relating to electrical discharges in gases, the specialists' terminology is generally avoided. In those areas where data and theories are considered inadequate the findings from man–made events and personal reasoning are introduced, thereby providing some original treatment – albeit, in part, of a speculative nature.

articleTitle: The role of interbar currents in squirrel cage motors having broken rotor bars
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper reviews the main aspects of the current monitoring technique for detecting broken rotor bars. Present techniques rely on the fact that a broken bar constitutes an open circuit, so that no current flows in this bar. The magnetic field in the machine is then unbalanced, giving rise to additional current sidebands in the frequency spectrum of the stator current around the fundamental component. The paper shows that significant interbar currents reduce any imbalance brought about by the broken bar. It is also shown experimentally that smaller imbalances do occur when interbar currents exist. An explanation for the above phenomena is provided, as well as a description of why it is necessary to look elsewhere in the current spectrum for a more reliable indication of broken bars.

articleTitle: An intelligent Internet platform and applications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The functions, specification and operation of a platform for the development of network service applications is described. Such applications are used to incorporate networking functions, such as bridging and network management into bridging devices in an internet. This provides the internet with autonomous intelligence distributed throughout the internet. The internet platform and application approach is unique in internetworking since it enables specific services or profiles to be handled as internet services rather than Application Layer services. The two novel applications described are innovative router-repeater bridging and direct multi-LAN traffic monitoring.

articleTitle: Modellering en spoedbeheer van 'n dieselkragopwekker vir vinnige lasverandering
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: UITTREKSEL 'n Blokdiagrammodel vir 'n dieselkragopwekker is ontwikkel. Die parameterwaardes van die blokdiagrammodel is bepaal deur middei van trapresponsietegnieke. Die blokdiagrammodel is gebruik om 'n vorentoevoer beheerder te ontwerp sodat die dieselkragopwekker se werkverrigting aan die gestelde vereistes voldoen.

articleTitle: Applied lightning research in an inter-tropical mountainous area
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents an overview on the lightning research and studies carried out by the Companhia Energética de Minas Gerais - CEMIG (Brazil), in its Lightning Research Programme. This Programme started with the measurement of the keraunic levels (number of thunderstorm days per year) and lightning current intensities on transmission, distribution and telecommunication towers, using magnetic links. Later the Programme was extended to include a lightning-flash counter network (cloud-to-ground flash densities), a lightning research station (Cachimbo Station) and a lightning detection and tracking system (LPATS). In parallel to this Programme, the CEMIG also undertook a systematic survey of soil resistivity and tower-footing resistances, as well as a survey on the lightning performance of power lines and telecommunication stations. The data obtained so far, especially from the research station and the tracking system, are considered as preliminary and are still being carefully analysed.

articleTitle: Using poynting vector theory to model and optimise power electronic switching
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Analysis of electromagnetic energy flux as depicted by the Poynting vector gives insight into the mechanism of power conditioning which is beyond the scope of classic circuit theory. Energy flux transmission is applied to switchmode electronic circuits and it will be shown that the characteristic impedance of connecting structures and components plays an important role during electromagnetic optimization of high frequency circuits.

articleTitle: A combined dyadic and matrix-trace technique for the design of multi-input control systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: For a single-input controllable system the solution of the pole-placement problem, (using a linear feedback combination of state variables), results in a unique set of feedback-weighting coefficients. These coefficients may be calculated by a number of methods including matrix trace techniques. For multi-input systems there are a theoretically infinite number of combinations of feedback coefficients that satisfy the pole-placement condition. In practice, the choice is much more limited if the feedback coefficients are to be of acceptable magnitudes; thus there is a need for constraining the problem so that a practical design is produced. A semi-systematic way of achieving this goal is via the dyadic method [1] in which the feedback matrix is a product of two dyads. If the value of one of these dyads is specified, this is tantamount to assigning a weighting on each of the inputs, then the other may be found systematically by way of a “fictitious” single-input system model. This paper uses the dyadic method, in combination with matrix-trace techniques, to design feedback systems for the longitudinal flight dynamics of a helicopter, an observer for a single-input system (observer design is usually a multi-input problem), and to achieve both zero- and pole-placement for a particular, restricted class of system.

articleTitle: Successful combinations of software engineering strategy and project management
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The emphasis on improving the productivity of software development activities has made the conventional approach to software development unpopular in some development environments. It is argued that the classical approach is valid only if the customer can afford to wait a long time for the completion of the project, and then only if the user requirements are stable over this long period. As a result, rapid approaches to software development (where many activities are conducted in parallel) have become popular. Successful control and execution of projects is facilitated if the conventional approach is adopted. However, as the conventional approach becomes unpopular, so too do the formal approaches to management - approaches which provide effective control. The combination of rapid, parallel software development activities and informal management techniques creates conditions that are not conducive to successful project execution, and could lead to chaotic development efforts. This paper investigates the characteristics of software development activities and management approaches, and proposes a model of Situational Software Engineering that provides guidance as to the most appropriate choice in a given situation.

articleTitle: An experimental evaluation of various continuous-time system identification methods
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Various integral based least-squares methods which identify the coefficients of continuous-time differential equation models from sampled data have been proposed. The behaviour of three of these methods is investigated under practical experimental conditions. Recommendations are given as to the use of the various methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of the regenerative undeland snubber circuit and its load effects
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper the influence of a particular snubber circuit on voltage source inverter loads is investigated. The switching transients of an inverter leg, equipped with the turn-on and turn-off snubber as proposed by Undeland and Marquardt, are analyzed for the completely regenerative case. The results are used to calculate the asymmetrical output voltages of a three phase inverter. The implications of the asymmetry for motor drives are discussed. The relative importance of dead time and the influence of snubber circuits on output voltage distortion are treated. The results are confirmed by measurements.
